criteria.statement: A G4 approval cannot authorize a later source commit; a fresh synthetic fixture approval restores only that fixture's transition.
A preplanted temporary hardlink cannot redirect atomic publication onto an outside sentinel.
Fast-lane validation can execute a recorded child Aegis operation without holding its parent state lease.
The actual lane cap changes, malformed limits/paths refuse, and unknown app scopes do not mutate the root pipeline.

review_provenance: Scoped fresh-context model reviews plus conductor reconciliation and runnable regressions. Not an independent human security certification or G4 approval.

findings.summary: State, memory, path-ownership and recovery findings were repaired, re-reviewed and independently reverified by the conductor; the ledger links their negative controls.
Ref aliases, nested recovery identities, malformed receipts, mutable source checks and competing-result false passes have explicit regression coverage and repairs.
Fresh builds, built-asset packaging, caller-owned source approval and accurate scope/limitations replace the prior misleading release paths. Final CI, artifact and human gates are still required.

Legacy strict flags, structural doc heuristics, unavailable host capabilities, power-loss durability and comparative/small-executor effectiveness retain the limits stated in the release contract and queued v0.11 plan.
